notes: Copilot is a NATIVE self-prompting loop, not an externally-driven one: `/autopilot on` puts the session in autopilot mode and, on every session.idle, tryAutopilotContinuation dispatches its own next prompt (app.js:2398) until the model calls task_complete or --max-autopilot-continues (default 5) is hit. The driver therefore sends EXACTLY ONE prompt for the whole run, and iter2_start is the load-bearing phase: a ready→working transition on the same session with no driver input between it and iter1_end can only have come from copilot re-prompting itself. Each continuation is emitted as a real user.message (the system.notification branch of the shared prompt path needs a notificationKind, which the autopilot send does not supply — app.js:2421), carrying source:"system", agentMode:"autopilot" and EMPTY content; parser.go maps it to EventType user_message → working, and the explicit assistant.turn_end marker settles each iteration → ready. The spec's strict 'stays continuously working' bullet is relaxed exactly as the claudecode sibling relaxed it — continuations fire AFTER turn_end, so the session flickers ready↔working per iteration — and what is asserted instead is the per-iteration arc, the unprompted second iteration, and the no-waiting invariant (--allow-all pre-approves every tool, so permission.requested is structurally unreachable). PRESESSION SHAPE: copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch holding only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so processlifecycle mints a proc-<PID> row first and the real session arrives under a DIFFERENT id — birth is two phases and every later phase anchors to the real session, templated from the copilot basic-turn sibling. Each iterN_end anchors to its own iterN_start (not to session_birth) so the matcher picks the post-iteration ready rather than the birth ready. OBSERVATIONS: cost and tokens are both live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map; model is NOT pinned because --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn. PROVISIONAL: daemon=full rests on the continuation being emitted as user.message, which is code-evidenced but not yet recording-evidenced — if the recording shows iter2_start missing, the session sat in ready for the entire autonomous run and this cell is daemon=bug.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
Real <session-id> session reconciles under a different session id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, born ready
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)
Spec bullet 1 — 'ready → working at loop start': the single driver prompt sets the objective while the session is already in autopilot mode (user.message → working)
First autonomous iteration completes: assistant.turn_end settles the turn → ready. session.idle then fires and tryAutopilotContinuation plans the next self-prompt

THE AUTONOMY ASSERTION — spec bullet 3, 'agent generates and executes its own next steps with no user prompts': the same session goes ready → working again with NO driver input in between. The driver's script sends exactly one prompt for the whole run, so this transition can only be copilot's own autopilot continuation (a user.message with source system, agentMode autopilot and empty content). If this phase fails, the continuation never reached the transcript and the session sat in ready for the rest of the autonomous run
Second autonomous iteration completes → back to ready; the loop either continues or terminates on task_complete

Spec bullet 6 — 'after the goal is reached: working → ready'. The loop ends on its own (the model calls task_complete, which also flips the mode back to interactive, or the --max-autopilot-continues cap is hit) and the session's final state is ready. Across the whole autonomous run the session never entered waiting: the driver launches with --allow-all, so no permission.requested is ever written and waiting is structurally unreachable
